heroThesis: I turn questions from the bedside into
heroIntro: Neurology physician and clinical researcher at Korea University Medical Center. My work spans acute stroke, memory disorders, and data-driven methods that make treatment decisions more precise in real-world practice.
aboutLead: I am interested in the moments when a clinical decision is necessary but the evidence is incomplete: when to begin antiplatelet therapy, how a new Alzheimer’s treatment behaves outside a trial, or what genetics can reveal about stroke severity.
aboutSupport: My approach combines neurological training with large clinical datasets, statistics, and reproducible analysis. The aim is simple: research that remains useful when it returns to the clinic.
futureCopy: My long-term goal is to integrate multiple genomic datasets with deeply phenotyped clinical cohorts to study neurological disease across the spectrum — from Alzheimer’s disease and other neurodegenerative disorders to stroke. I want to connect causal genetics, biomarkers, and real-world outcomes to identify mechanisms that can ultimately guide prevention and treatment.
methodsCopy: Experience with large clinical datasets, effect estimates and confidence intervals, individual-level genotyping data, and supervised two-sample Mendelian randomization workflows.
contactTitle: Let’s talk about a clinical question worth answering.

researchAreas.title: Acute stroke & antithrombotic therapy
researchAreas.copy: Using large, real-world stroke registries to ask when treatment begins to matter — with a focus on minor stroke, high-risk TIA, and dual antiplatelet therapy.

researchAreas.title: Memory disorders & disease-modifying therapy
researchAreas.copy: Studying how emerging therapies translate from trials into clinical practice, including safety, ARIA risk, and early treatment patterns with lecanemab.

researchAreas.title: Clinical & genomic data science
researchAreas.copy: Connecting clinical registries with survival analysis, causal inference, and genetic data to answer questions that remain grounded in patient care.

workingProjects.status: Review article · Forthcoming in Journal of Stroke
workingProjects.title: Mendelian Randomization for the Stroke Clinician: What It Can and Cannot Tell Us
workingProjects.copy: A clinically oriented review of Mendelian randomization in stroke: what it assumes, how its estimates should be interpreted, where it can help prioritize therapeutic targets, and where clinical translation can go wrong.

workingProjects.title: Migraine and stroke: shared genomic architecture
